questions.question: A single server serves jobs one at a time in order of arrival (FIFO) and never idles while a job is present; job $k$ arrives at $A_k$, needs service time $S_k$, starts service at $\tilde{A}_k$ and departs at $D_k$, with $D_0=0$. Which formula gives the start of service $\tilde{A}_k$ of job $k$?

A single server serves jobs one at a time in order of arrival (FIFO) and never idles while a job is present; job $k$ arrives at $A_k$, needs service time $S_k$, starts service at $\tilde{A}_k$ and departs at $D_k$, with $D_0=0$. Exactly when does job $k$ have a positive waiting time $W_k=\tilde{A}_k-A_k$?

A single server serves jobs one at a time in order of arrival (FIFO) and never idles while a job is present; job $k$ arrives at $A_k$, needs service time $S_k$, starts service at $\tilde{A}_k$ and departs at $D_k$, with $D_0=0$. The first job arrives at $A_1\geq 0$. What does the start value $D_0=0$ imply for job 1?
options: Service begins at time $0$, giving a wait of $-A_1$.
Job 1 waits for a job 0 that departs at $D_0$.

questions.question: A single server serves jobs one at a time in order of arrival (FIFO) and never idles while a job is present; job $k$ arrives at $A_k$, needs service time $S_k$, starts service at $\tilde{A}_k$ and departs at $D_k$, with $D_0=0$. Why is $D_{k-1}$ the only departure epoch that enters the start of service of job $k$?
options: Because the service times are i.i.d., all earlier jobs take equally long.
Because jobs $1,\ldots,k-2$ always leave before job $k$ arrives.
Because a non-idling server always has $D_{k-1}=A_k$.
Because with one FIFO server, job $k-1$ is the last job served before job $k$.

questions.question: A single server serves jobs one at a time in order of arrival (FIFO) and never idles while a job is present; job $k$ arrives at $A_k$, needs service time $S_k$, starts service at $\tilde{A}_k$ and departs at $D_k$, with $D_0=0$. Which inequality between successive departure epochs holds on every sample path?
At a single FIFO server that never idles while work is present, job 1 departs at $D_1=45$ minutes. Job 2 arrives at $A_2=25$ and needs $S_2=15$ minutes of service. What is its departure epoch $D_2$?
At a single FIFO server that never idles while work is present, job 2 departs at $D_2=9$. Job 3 arrives at $A_3=12$ with service time $S_3=4$. What is its waiting time $W_3=\tilde{A}_3-A_3$?

A single FIFO server that never idles while work is present starts empty. Inter-arrival times are $X=(2,1)$ and service times $S=(4,2)$, so $A_k=A_{k-1}+X_k$ with $A_0=0$. What is the sojourn time $J_2=D_2-A_2$ of job 2?

At a single FIFO server that never idles while work is present and starts empty, four jobs arrive at $A=(0,3,4,10)$ with service times $S=(4,2,3,1)$. Apart from job 1, which job starts service at its own arrival epoch?
At a single FIFO server that never idles while work is present, job $k$ arrives at $A_k=9$, needs $S_k=5$ and departs at $D_k=17$. What is its waiting time $W_k$?

A single server serves jobs one at a time in order of arrival (FIFO) and never idles while a job is present; job $k$ arrives at $A_k$, needs service time $S_k$, starts service at $\tilde{A}_k$ and departs at $D_k$, with $D_0=0$. A student writes $D_k=D_{k-1}+S_k$ instead of the full recursion. For which jobs does this shortcut give the correct departure epoch?
options: Exactly for the jobs with $A_k\leq D_{k-1}$
Exactly for jobs arriving at an idle server, after $D_{k-1}$
For every job, as the server never idles
Only for job 1, since it finds the system empty

questions.question: At one FIFO server that cannot idle while work is waiting, job $k$ arrives at $A_k$ and job $k-1$ departs at $D_{k-1}$. Which statement about the start of service $\tilde{A}_k$ of job $k$ is correct?
options: $\tilde{A}_k\geq A_k$ and $\tilde{A}_k\geq D_{k-1}$, with exactly one of them an equality
$\tilde{A}_k\geq A_k$ and $\tilde{A}_k\leq D_{k-1}$, so service starts by the previous departure
$\tilde{A}_k$ may be any epoch with $\tilde{A}_k\geq A_k$ and $\tilde{A}_k\geq D_{k-1}$
$\tilde{A}_k\geq A_k$ and $\tilde{A}_k\geq D_{k-1}$, with at least one of them an equality

questions.question: A FIFO system has two identical servers, each serving one job at a time and never idling while jobs wait. Job $k$ arrives at $A_k$ and job $k-1$ departs at $D_{k-1}$. Why can $\tilde{A}_k=\max\{A_k,D_{k-1}\}$ give the wrong start of service?
options: It is still correct, since FIFO keeps the jobs in arrival order.
It is wrong only if the service times are not identically distributed.
Job $k$ may start as soon as either server is free, possibly before $D_{k-1}$.
Job $k$ must also wait for $D_{k-2}$, so the maximum must include it.

questions.question: A simulation of a single FIFO server stores the list $[D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3,D_4]=[0,2,5,9,14]$, where $D_0=0$ is the start value of the departure recursion and $D_1,\ldots,D_4$ are the departure epochs of four jobs. What is the mean departure epoch of the four jobs?
A single FIFO server that never idles while work is present starts empty. Three jobs arrive at $A=(1,2,3)$ with service times $S=(3,3,1)$. What is the average waiting time $\frac{1}{3}(W_1+W_2+W_3)$?

A single FIFO server that never idles while work is present starts empty. Jobs arrive at $A=(0,1,4,6)$ with service times $S=(3,2,1,3)$, which gives $D=(3,5,6,9)$. The workload at time $t$ is $[D_{A(t)}-t]^+$, where $A(t)$ is the number of arrivals in $[0,t]$. What is the workload at $t=4.5$?

A single server serves jobs one at a time in order of arrival (FIFO) and never idles while a job is present; job $k$ arrives at $A_k$, needs service time $S_k$, starts service at $\tilde{A}_k$ and departs at $D_k$, with $D_0=0$. For a system that starts empty, assume as induction hypothesis $D_{n-1}=\max_{1\leq j\leq n-1}\bigl(A_j+S_j+\cdots+S_{n-1}\bigr)$. Which step proves $D_n=\max_{1\leq j\leq n}\bigl(A_j+S_j+\cdots+S_n\bigr)$?
options: $D_n=D_{n-1}+S_n$, so adding $S_n$ to every candidate for $D_{n-1}$ gives all candidates
$D_n=\max\{A_n,D_{n-1}+S_n\}$, so $A_n$ joins the candidates as the term $j=n$
$D_n=\max\{A_n+S_n,D_{n-1}+S_n\}$, and $S_n$ is added to every candidate inside $D_{n-1}$
$D_n=\max\{A_n,D_{n-1}\}+S_n$, and $A_n\geq A_j$ makes the term $j=n$ the largest

questions.question: A single server serves jobs one at a time in order of arrival (FIFO) and never idles while a job is present; job $k$ arrives at $A_k$, needs service time $S_k$, starts service at $\tilde{A}_k$ and departs at $D_k$, with $D_0=0$. With inter-arrival times $X_k=A_k-A_{k-1}$ and waiting times $W_k=\tilde{A}_k-A_k$, which recursion for $W_k$, $k\geq 2$, follows from $\tilde{A}_k=\max\{A_k,D_{k-1}\}$?

A single FIFO server that never idles while work is present starts empty. Five jobs arrive at $A=(0,2,3,8,9)$ with service times $S=(4,1,2,3,1)$. In $D_5=\max_{1\leq j\leq 5}\bigl(A_j+S_j+\cdots+S_5\bigr)$, which job attains the maximum, and what is $D_5$?

A single FIFO server that never idles while work is present starts empty. Jobs arrive at $A=(0,1,2,8)$ with service times $S=(2,2,2,1)$, giving $D=(2,4,6,9)$. If $S_1$ is increased from $2$ to $5$, by how much does each of $D_1,D_2,D_3,D_4$ increase?
